clue.text: Hero-subject due for a change as novel stonemason

indicators.note: letters due for a change are to be rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A heroic subject is ripe for revision, as a novel about a stonemason shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges the fourteen letters of HERO-SUBJECT and DUE. Thomas Hardy's novel takes its title from its hero, Jude Fawley, a stonemason.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy titled his novel after its protagonist, a working stonemason, so the title names both book and man.

clue.text: Kitty with fellow taking cannabis

parts.note: jack is an old word for a man or fellow
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A man smoking dope beside the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money in a game, the prize fund also called the pot.

clue.text: Refugee from clan predisposed to scatter

indicators.note: the letters are made to scatter and land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing a family group that was inclined to break apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to scatter' rearranges the fifteen letters of CLAN and PREDISPOSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone driven from home, the official postwar term being a displaced person.

clue.text: Excessively long bill, for example?

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: An overlong invoice, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A bill here is a billhook, a cutting implement, not an invoice; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A billhook is a hand implement for cutting branches, an instance of a workman's implement.

clue.text: Force used by thief for tampering

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Violence employed by a burglar meddling with a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort and force both mean exertion of strength, as in putting force or effort into a push.

clue.text: For example, Bede is represented as overwhelmed with requests

indicators.note: Bede is represented as something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Venerable Bede, say, is portrayed as swamped by petitioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is represented as' rearranges EG with BEDE and IS; the IS belongs to the fodder via the indicator phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mobbed by petitioners is figuratively besieged, surrounded as a castle is by an army.

clue.text: Presentation of a tot?

parts.note: a tot is a small child, and its presentation is its first appearance in the world rather than a small measure of rum being served

explanation.definitionFit: A baby is first presented to the world at its delivery by its mother.

clue.text: Brushing-up studies, say

parts.note: brushing up means revising old knowledge, and a short course of study does that; the say hints at a further sense of a second drink or helping at a meal

explanation.definitionFit: A short course for updating skills is the standard name for revision training.

clue.text: Tricky question for Badger-and Ratty, initially

parts.note: to badger is to pester or tease

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of Ratty

explanation.surface: A puzzle set for the Badger and Ratty of The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger and Ratty are characters in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, but here 'Badger' is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a puzzle or tricky problem posed to someone.

clue.text: Shed, substandard, is abandoned

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin
off means below standard, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A hut, poorly built, has been left derelict.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-off things are discarded, given up by their owner as no longer wanted.

clue.text: Breathe through nose very loudly in Neil's trouble

indicators.note: in places the musical mark for very loudly within the other letters
the letters of Neil's are troubled, stirred into a new order

parts.note: the name and its S give the five letters to be rearranged
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Neil's problem makes him snort noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges NEILS to SNILE, and 'in' puts FF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sniff repeatedly through the nostrils, as with a cold, is to snuffle or sniffle.

clue.text: Large building foundation

explanation.surface: A big structure's base.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand house can be called a stately pile, and a pile is also a post driven into the ground to support a structure.

clue.text: Day interminable with no one to turn to

definitions.text: with no one to turn to

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
endless means interminable, never stopping

explanation.surface: An endless day spent alone with nobody to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without companions has nobody to rely on or ask for help.

clue.text: Choose to make a speech for all voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to deliver a formal speech

explanation.surface: A candidate decides to address the whole voting public.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of people entitled to vote in an election makes up the constituency's voters.

clue.text: Apply oneself to rigging

explanation.surface: Get stuck into the ship's ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to grips with a task is to tackle it, and a ship's ropes and pulleys are its tackle.

clue.text: Explain crack?

explanation.surface: Make clear what a fissure is.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out the meaning of something obscure explains it, and to break a code is to crack it.

clue.text: Ivy, for example, wearing Sunday shoes

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant, a kind of creeper

explanation.surface: Ivy dressed up in its Sunday best footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Brothel creepers are thick-soled suede shoes of 1950s British fashion; 'wearing' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe-soled suede footwear is popularly called brothel creepers, or just creepers.

clue.text: Cocktails taken in combinations?

explanation.surface: Mixed drinks consumed in mixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: A combination in Britain is a motorcycle with a passenger car attached, so it carries one.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy, orange-liqueur and lemon drink shares its name with the passenger pod bolted to a motorbike in a combination.

clue.text: Private papers sorted out

indicators.note: papers sorted out are shuffled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Confidential documents put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' is not secret but the soldier's rank: a sapper is a private in the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a lowest-rank soldier of the army's engineers, digging trenches and saps.

clue.text: Celebrity goes to church with such formality

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person attends a service with great ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiffness of manner, as in a starchy, stiff person.

clue.text: Means of fixing locks out of the rain

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the rain are turned out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something to keep the hair dry when caught in a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the hair holds a hairstyle in place.

clue.text: California prohibit a changing-but on the beach?

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
to ban is to prohibit

explanation.surface: A Californian rule bans beach huts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabana is a small shelter or cabin by a beach or pool where bathers undress.

clue.text: Remarkable new name in carbolic acid

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the chemical's name

parts.note: phenol is the chemical name for carbolic acid

indicators.note: new makes the letters of name into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh label on a disinfectant bottle is extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NAME to MENA, and 'in' puts it inside PHENOL after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phenomenal is extraordinary, beyond the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: Work in it back to front as some protection from sun

indicators.note: in places the work abbreviation inside the turned word
back to front says the word it is read in reverse

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Wearing something backwards to shade the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' turns IT to TI, and 'in' puts OP inside. A topi is a pith helmet worn in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet shields the wearer's head from tropical heat.

clue.text: Dismal conservative?

explanation.surface: A gloomy Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is feeling blue, and the UK Conservative Party's colour is blue, so a Tory is a true-blue.

clue.text: Enthrall, in French style, with Valse Exotique

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: exotic suggests the letters of the waltz are rearranged unusually

explanation.surface: Captivate, in French fashion, with an exotic waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotique' rearranges VALSE (French for waltz) to SLAVE; 'style' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral someone originally meant to make them a thrall, a bondsman, so to enslave.

clue.text: Oil near out? There's a banking flap!

indicators.note: out says the letters of oil near are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Running out of fuel causes panic at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' is an aircraft tilting in a turn, not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged surface on an aircraft wing tilts the plane into a turn.

clue.text: Demurest tenant thrown out for litotes

indicators.note: thrown out means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The meekest lodger evicted for using litotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges DEMUREST and TENANT. Litotes is a figure of speech saying less than meant, as in 'not bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech that plays something down, such as calling a fortune not bad.
